# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 42 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 42 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_042_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

Mandate 11 is the most important text in Hermas for understanding second-century prophecy and its discernment. Two settings are contrasted: the false prophet operates in a private consultation (like a *mantis*, a diviner), while the true prophet operates exclusively within the assembled congregation (*ekklēsia*). The key discernment criterion is location and context, not content alone.

The false prophet is described as *kenos* — empty — three times in 42:2, creating a rhetorical pattern. The "angel of the prophetic Spirit" (*angelos tou pneumatos tou prophetikou*) who "rests upon" the prophet is a distinctive angelomorphic pneumatology that does not exactly parallel Paul's formulations.

EMET renders *mantis* as "diviner"; LOGOS as "soothsayer"; PNEUMA as "fortune-teller." SOPHIA uses "diviner" — a more neutral technical term that acknowledges Hermas's contrast between legitimate and illegitimate oracular practice.

---

## Mandate 11, Part 1 — True and False Prophets

**42:1** He showed me men seated on a bench and another man seated in a chair. He said to me: "Do you see the men seated on the bench?" "I see them, lord," I replied. "These," he said, "are the faithful; and he who sits in the chair is a false prophet who is destroying the understanding of the servants of God — that is, of the double-minded, not of the faithful."

**42:2** "These double-minded persons come to him as to a diviner and consult him about what will happen to them. And that false prophet, having no power of the divine Spirit within himself, speaks with them according to their inquiries and the desires of their wicked hearts, and fills their souls as they desire. For being empty himself, he gives empty answers to those who are empty. For whatever word is asked of him, he speaks — he speaks from the emptiness of his own heart. Yet at times he happens to speak some word correctly, because the devil fills him so that some of his words may come true, in order that this prophet may have the greater confidence and that the double-minded may flock to him in greater numbers, so that he may lead them the more effectively astray."

**42:3** "All those who are strong in the faith of the Lord do not consult him, knowing that there is no truth in him. For no spirit given by God requires to be questioned; but since it possesses the power of the divine, it speaks of itself, because it speaks as God wills. Therefore when the man who has the divine Spirit comes into an assembly of righteous men who have faith in the divine Spirit, and the assembly of those men offers prayer, then the angel of the prophetic Spirit, who rests upon him, fills that man, and the man, being filled with the Holy Spirit, speaks to the congregation as the Lord wills."

**42:4** "In this way the divine Spirit will be made manifest. Whatever power, therefore, the divine Spirit has to speak — that power is of the Lord. Hear therefore concerning the Spirit that is from God and concerning the false spirit, so that you may believe in the true Spirit and not put your trust in the false one."

---

*SOPHIA represents the consensus rendering of EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA, with rulings recorded in the Disagreement Log.*
